memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If you offer an animal from the flock as a fellowship offering to the LORD, you are to offer a male or female without defect. If you offer a lamb, you are to present it before the LORD, lay your hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting. Then Aaron's sons shall splash its blood against the sides of the altar.'" - Lev 3:6-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once again the offering scales down. From the herd to the flock — from cattle to a lamb. Once again, God has made room for the household with less.

By now this pattern should be familiar. Chapter 1 did it. Chapter 2 did it. Chapter 3 does it again. God keeps opening the door wider.

And once again, what does not change is the requirement: without defect. Lay your hand on its head. Blood against the altar. The lesser cost does not mean a lesser standard of holiness or a lesser act of substitution.

There is something reassuring about how repetitive Leviticus is on this point. God is patiently establishing in His people's minds that access to Him is genuinely available to everyone, and genuinely serious for everyone.

The New Testament carries both truths forward. Whoever comes to me I will never drive away, Jesus said (Jn 6:37) — that is the open door. And be holy, because I am holy, God says to His people (1 Pet 1:15-16) — that is the unchanging standard. Grace does not lower the standard. Christ meets it on our behalf.

Come with what you have. Come as you are. But know who you are coming to.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I let the size of my offering make me feel less welcome before God?
2. Do I hold together both God's open welcome and His holiness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that the door to You is wide and the way to You is holy. Thank You that Christ satisfies both. Amen.
